--- title: "Introduction" --- - Vital to understand data before analyzing it - Is coding correct? Is distribution skewed? Are there clear relationships between variables? Etc. - These types of questions are easy to answer/process visually - The human brain can much more quickly understand visual information than numerical or textual information ([Medina 2008](https://brainrules.net/)) :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} *"The graphical method has considerable superiority for the exposition of statistical facts over the tabular. A heavy bank of figures is grievously wearisome to the eye, and the popular mind is as incapable of drawing any useful lessons from it as of extracting sunbeams from cucumbers." ([Farquhar and Farquhar 1891](https://books.google.com/books?hl=en&lr=&id=7bYIMv0XgfsC&oi=fnd&pg=PA1&dq=Farquhar+and+Farquhar+1891&ots=9N2es-pjK0&sig=8SWt5cnWvswmI_1OQSa3wwv7LCw#v=onepage&q=Farquhar%20and%20Farquhar%201891&f=false))* ::: ::: {.column width="45%"} ![](images/sunbeams.jpeg){width=45% fig-alt="Bright yellow sunbeams radiating from a center point."} ![](images/gullivers-travels.jpeg){width=45% fig-alt="Poster for the 1977 film Gulliver's Travels."} ![](images/cucumber.jpeg){width=60% fig-alt="A sliced cucumber."} ::: :::: ## Assessing models via visualizations [Anscombe's (1973)](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00031305.1973.10478966) quartet ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . use "https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/anscombe.dta", clear . . tabstat Y* Xabc Xd, stat(mean sd min max) format(%4.2f) col(stats) Variable | Mean SD Min Max -------------+---------------------------------------- Yb | 7.50 2.03 3.10 9.26 Yc | 7.50 2.03 5.39 12.74 Yd | 7.50 2.03 5.25 12.50 Ya | 7.50 2.03 4.26 10.84 Xabc | 9.00 3.32 4.00 14.00 Xd | 9.00 3.32 8.00 19.00 ------------------------------------------------------ . . qui regress Ya Xabc . estimates store Ya . qui regress Yb Xabc . estimates store Yb . qui regress Yc Xabc . estimates store Yc . qui regress Yd Xd . estimates store Yd . . esttab Ya Yb Yc Yd, b(2) se(2) title("Linear Regression Estimates") Linear Regression Estimates ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- (1) (2) (3) (4) Ya Yb Yc Yd ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Xabc 0.50** 0.50** 0.50** (0.12) (0.12) (0.12) Xd 0.50** (0.12) _cons 3.00* 3.00* 3.00* 3.00* (1.12) (1.13) (1.12) (1.12) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- N 11 11 11 11 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Standard errors in parentheses * p<0.05, ** p<0.01, *** p<0.001 ``` ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(foreign) # load Stata datasets library(ggplot2) # main graphics package library(modelsummary) # coefficient plots & nice tables library(cleanplots) # Mize's graphics scheme ## Use cleanplots colors, markers, lines, and theme for all graphs ## cleanplots_defaults() theme_update(plot.title.position = "plot") # titles start at left edge of graph # Anscombe's quartet anscombe <- read.dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/anscombe.dta") summary(anscombe[c("Ya", "Yb", "Yc", "Yd")]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` r-output Ya Yb Yc Yd Min. : 4.260 Min. :3.100 Min. : 5.39 Min. : 5.250 1st Qu.: 6.315 1st Qu.:6.695 1st Qu.: 6.25 1st Qu.: 6.170 Median : 7.580 Median :8.140 Median : 7.11 Median : 7.040 Mean : 7.501 Mean :7.501 Mean : 7.50 Mean : 7.501 3rd Qu.: 8.570 3rd Qu.:8.950 3rd Qu.: 7.98 3rd Qu.: 8.190 Max. :10.840 Max. :9.260 Max. :12.74 Max. :12.500 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} amod1 <- lm(Ya ~ Xabc, data = anscombe) amod2 <- lm(Yb ~ Xabc, data = anscombe) amod3 <- lm(Yc ~ Xabc, data = anscombe) amod4 <- lm(Yd ~ Xd, data = anscombe) modelsummary(list(amod1, amod2, amod3, amod4), stars = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

All y & x Variables Have Same Mean and S > D") ``` ![](fig/dmv-00_a-anscombe.png){width=80% fig-alt="[0.a] Scatterplot of Anscombe's four y variables against x, each set in its own color and marker: the sets follow different patterns even though their summary statistics are the same."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 0.a - Scatterplot of the data ggplot(anscombe) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Ya), color = cleanplots_colors("red"), size = 3) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Yb), color = cleanplots_colors("ltblue"), size = 3) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Yc), color = cleanplots_colors("gray"), size = 3) + geom_point(aes(x = Xd, y = Yd), color = cleanplots_colors("black"), size = 3) + labs(x = "X", y = "Y", title = "[0.a] Anscombe's quartet - All y & x variables have same mean and SD") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](introduction_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-alt='[0.a] Scatterplot of Anscombe\'s four y variables against x, each set in its own color: the sets follow different patterns even though their summary statistics are the same.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: ::: {.panel-tabset group="language"} ## Stata ```{.stata-run} . // 0.b - Add connected lines . twoway /// > (connected Ya Xabc) /// > (connected Yb Xabc) /// > (connected Yc Xabc) /// > (scatter Yd Xd), /// > ylab(0(5)15) xlab(0(5)20) /// > title("[0.b] Anscombe's Quartet - All y & x Variables Have Same Mean and S > D") ``` ![](fig/dmv-00_b-anscombe_lines.png){width=80% fig-alt="[0.b] The same scatterplot with lines connecting the points of the first three sets: one set rises roughly linearly with noise, one is a smooth upside-down U, and one is a straight line with a single outlier; the fourth set has all but one point at the same x value."} ## R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # 0.b - Add connected lines ggplot(anscombe) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Ya), color = cleanplots_colors("red"), size = 3) + geom_line( aes(x = Xabc, y = Ya), color = cleanplots_colors("red")) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Yb), color = cleanplots_colors("ltblue"), size = 3) + geom_line( aes(x = Xabc, y = Yb), color = cleanplots_colors("ltblue")) + geom_point(aes(x = Xabc, y = Yc), color = cleanplots_colors("gray"), size = 3) + geom_line( aes(x = Xabc, y = Yc), color = cleanplots_colors("gray")) + geom_point(aes(x = Xd, y = Yd), color = cleanplots_colors("black"), size = 3) + labs(x = "X", y = "Y", title = "[0.b] Anscombe's quartet - All y & x variables have same mean and SD") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](introduction_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-alt='[0.b] The same scatterplot with lines connecting the points of the first three sets: one set rises roughly linearly with noise, one is a smooth upside-down U, and one is a straight line with a single outlier; the fourth set has all but one point at the same x value.' width=80%} ::: ::: ::: :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/mcap-illustration.png){fig-alt="The Methodology Center illustration: small line drawings of graphs around a central MCAP circle."} ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ![](images/anscombe-mcap-original.png){fig-alt="The Anscombe line plot that one of the Methodology Center illustration's small drawings is based on."} ::: :::: \*[Read about The Methodology Center graphic](https://www.purdue.edu/research/mcap/illustration/) ## Good data visualization balances art and science *"Data visualization is part art and part science. The challenge is to get the art right without getting the science wrong, and vice versa." ([Wilke 2019](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/) p.1)* :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Too many data visualization guides lean on aesthetic opinions only - Aesthetics are important... - But there is a large scientific literature on what makes an **effective** data visualization - Goal is to learn general principles to guide any data or model visualization - To make visualizations that are both effective and beautiful - Along the way, add to your toolbox of visualization strategies - Learn what tools are effective for what types of data and situations ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ![](images/wes-anderson-palette.jpeg){fig-alt="The Wes Anderson film color palette: rows of colored bars for The Royal Tenenbaums, Rushmore, The Life Aquatic, and Fantastic Mr. Fox."} ![](images/fantastic-mr-fox.jpeg){width=70% fig-alt="Poster for Fantastic Mr. Fox."} ::: ::::
